location: UKL net pens, Rattlesnake Point (UKLN & UKLS)
cause_description_in_file: Suspected avian (bird) predators infiltrating net pen netting
citation_and_page: FY2024 Annual Report, p. 28; FY2023 Annual Report, p. 21; FY2023 Annual Report, p. 25; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 17
issues: Counts and survival match the table; total 1,014 and ~99.0% pooled loss are derived by arithmetic. Predation is only suspected in the report.
suggested_cause_description: Suspected avian predators may have infiltrated the netting in 2019; survival 0.0% (UKLN, 0/534) and 2.1% (UKLS, 10/480).

cause_description_in_file: Ammonia spike from staff raising pond temps above 15C via increased geothermal flow to extend growing season
issues: Report gives no Dec-Feb mortality dates; says 'ammonia increase' with chronic low-level mortality, not a spike; 'outdoor' not stated; no counts.
suggested_cause_description: Winter 2020/21 production season: increased geothermal flows to raise pond temperatures above 15C to extend the growing season led to a marked increase in total ammonia and chronic low-level mortality in ponds holding CY2019 fish (7,664 fish going into winter).

cause_description_in_file: Unknown; suspected unstable incubation water temperature or jar agitation, later suspected geothermal water chemistry (low hardness/alkalinity, dissolved metals)
citation_and_page: FY2021 Annual Report, p. 13; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 6
issues: Date is the spawning night, not the loss; cause was suspected, not unknown; SNARRC figure is hatch rate not survival.
suggested_cause_description: Suspected unstable incubation water temperature or excessive agitation in hatching jars; later raised possible geothermal water chemistry (low hardness/alkalinity, dissolved metals). All eggs incubated at the hatchery perished during hatch.

cause_description_in_file: Unknown; suspected geothermal water chemistry despite improved temperature control
citation_and_page: FY2021 Annual Report, p. 13; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 6
issues: Date is the spawning date; trays were borrowed heath trays on a small recirculation system; report notes weak hatch then total losses within days of hatch.
suggested_cause_description: Cause not known; not likely temperature related despite tighter control; possible geothermal water chemistry (low hardness/alkalinity, dissolved metals).

cause_description_in_file: Gut impaction from fry ingesting unhatched Artemia cysts during early feeding
issues: Report calls it a feeding problem, not disease. Report does not attribute the 50.2% survival to E05/E06; that figure covers all losses from collection to ponding. Location only 'tanks'.
suggested_cause_description: Gut impaction from fry ingesting unhatched Artemia cysts during early feeding (mid-May), causing significant mortalities; not separately quantified. Overall collection-to-ponding survival 50.2% (53,518 of 106,710) includes all causes.

cause_description_in_file: Costia (parasitic protozoan) outbreak
issues: 'Parasitic protozoan' not in report; tank location not stated; 50.2% not attributed to this event.
suggested_cause_description: Costia outbreak in mid-June caused significant loss of fry; not separately quantified.

cause_description_in_file: Drought / low reservoir water levels; projected to go dry within weeks
citation_and_page: FY2021 Annual Report, p. 16; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 17; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 7
issues: 0.0% loss is wrong: 2,175 of 2,479 stocked (87.7% survival), so ~12.3% not recovered. 'Within weeks' is the compiler's wording (report says dry by about early August). FY2023/FY2024 say early July harvest vs mid-July here.
suggested_cause_description: Gerber net pen expected to go dry by about early August under drought; emergency harvest in mid-July recovered 2,175 of 2,479 fish (87.7% survival; ~12.3% not recovered) and stocked them to refugia in Upper Klamath Lake.

location: Upper Klamath Lake net pens (UKLN total loss; UKLS partial)
cause_description_in_file: Anoxic conditions for several consecutive nights, traced to USGS Rattlesnake Point monitoring
citation_and_page: FY2021 Annual Report, p. 16; FY2021 Annual Report, p. 17
issues: UKLS survival figures 34.8%/23.1% are the combined-pen year-class values; Table 8 shows UKLS 58.0%/38.4% (40.4% total). 'Late July' not stated. 'Several nights' and 'traced to monitoring' are loose paraphrases.
suggested_cause_description: Large-scale mortality noted during a weekly check in early August, traced to several consecutive water quality events causing anoxia in early morning hours near the USGS Rattlesnake Point station. 606 of 2,500 recovered (24.2% survival; 75.8% loss); UKLN 0.0% survival; UKLS 40.4% (58.0% CY2019, 38.4% CY2020).

cause_description_in_file: Unknown; USFWS CA/NV Fish Health Center found no infectious agents; fish showed tetany with lateral bruising
issues: Table 3/4 parenthetical unsupported (A2/A4 not in FY2022 Tables; appear in FY2023 tables pp.18-19); 'outdoor A-series' and 'larval' are inferred; 'disease' category not supported (no infectious agent)
suggested_cause_description: Unknown; USFWS CA/NV Fish Health Center found no infectious agents; many fish showed tetany with lateral bruising; chronic mortality Aug-Sept until ponds cooled in Oct.

cause_description_in_file: Tetany (cause unknown) plus gill lamellae necrosis from winter thermal complications
issues: 'thermal' not stated (report says complications with winter lamellae thickening); 'disease' category questionable; report calls it a 'small' event and notes salt bath treatment
suggested_cause_description: Small mortality event in Pond P9; no infectious agents found; tetany observed in several fish; some fish had gill lamellae necrosis due to complications with the winter thickening of lamellae; treated with salt bath.

location: In-transport, Agency Lake, en route to UKLW net pen
cause_description_in_file: High winds and large waves during boat transport
issues: 2,199 loaded not in any report (derived); 1,999 'arrived' is an interpretation; 9.1% is arithmetic; 'boat' not stated
suggested_cause_description: Estimated 200+ fish lost during transport across Agency Lake due to high winds and large waves (UKLW stocked 4/8/2022 with 1,999 fish).

location: UKLW & UKLE net pens, Four Mile Canal, Agency Lake
cause_description_in_file: Repeated DO crashes/anoxia (DO=0.0 mg/L on multiple dates; below 2 mg/L 20 times) compounded by heavy non-target bycatch (fathead minnow, tui chub, blue chub) competing for food -> low growth/emaciation
issues: Causal wording too strong (report: bycatch 'may have' and low DO 'can contribute'); loss percentages and 3,851 total are arithmetic; survival (47.9%) is the reported figure
suggested_cause_description: Net pen survival 47.9% (1,844 of 3,851); DO 0.0 mg/L on several dates and below 2 mg/L 20 times (7/29-8/25), heavy bycatch may have limited food; low growth, many emaciated fish. Highest net pen survival in program history.

cause_description_in_file: Low river flows reduced effectiveness of passive drift-net collection gear
issues: Not a mortality event (fine); 'weather' category not stated (low river flows); 'May-June' not tied to this statement, only 'early in the collection season'
suggested_cause_description: Low river flows led to ineffective passive drift-net catch rates early in the collection season, prompting a switch to active dip netting.

location: Fingerling growout pond - Bozeman Razorback (RZB) diet trial
cause_description_in_file: Suspected nutrition-related pathology: extreme gill hyperplasia, little/no feeding, poor visceral fat stores, protein loss in urine (feed tested, not rancid)
citation_and_page: FY2023 Annual Report, p. 32; FY2023 Annual Report, p. 33
issues: 'Lowest of four diets' is wrong (STR 73% was lowest; RZB 86% was second lowest); 'suspected nutrition-related' not in report; 14.0% is derived from whole-treatment fingerling survival, not this event; 86% is end of fingerling stage; event is in FY2023 report, not FY2022
suggested_cause_description: Sporadic mortality began in one razorback-diet fingerling pond in Nov 2022; Fish Health Centers found extreme gill hyperplasia, little to no feeding, poor visceral fat and urinary protein loss in low-condition fish; feed was not rancid. Cause not stated. RZB end-of-fingerling survival 86% (STR 73%, JUN 87%, SHP 87%). Leave % lost blank.

cause_description_in_file: Possible high water temperatures plus tank overflow incidents
issues: Source is FY2023 report; 'Research Rack' and 'Spring-Summer' not stated (report says tanks, trial started May 2022); report words causes as 'possible high temperatures' and 'tank overflow issues'
suggested_cause_description: Larval stage of the diet trial was ended early after an increase in mortality from possible high temperatures and loss of larval fish to tank overflow; no conclusions drawn.

cause_description_in_file: Unspecified "fish health mortality event" (cause not further diagnosed in text)
citation_and_page: FY2023 Annual Report, p. 12; Table 3 p. 13
issues: (1) 'Indoor greenhouse' location not stated; (2) 80.3% loss is whole-tank loss (62.2% observed + 18.1% unobserved), not the Jul 2-4 event (752/1,509 = 49.8%); (3) '752 of 938' link is inferred; (4) cause not given (OK as 'unspecified'); 'disease' category is interpretation
suggested_cause_description: Fish health mortality event in Larval Tank C14, July 2-4, 2023: 752 fish died (cause not stated in the report). Tank C14 as a whole (1,509 collected 5/31) had 938 observed deaths and 19.7% overall survival (80.3% total loss incl. 18.1% unobserved).

location: UKL net pens, Four Mile Canal, Agency Lake (UKLW & UKLE)
cause_description_in_file: Anoxic conditions Jul-Sep, compounded by parasites, disease, secondary bacterial/hemorrhagic infection, and competition/crowding with fathead minnows and blue chubs
citation_and_page: FY2023 Annual Report, p. 23; p. 21; Table 8 p. 25
issues: 'Secondary bacterial' not stated (report: secondary infections in general, no field diagnostics); minnow/chub crowding is cited for 2022 and as a general concern (p. 21, 25), not as a 2023 cause; 97% loss is derived (report says 3.0% survival)
suggested_cause_description: Anoxic conditions (July-September) were a contributing factor; harvested fish were emaciated with parasites, disease and petechial hemorrhaging (no field diagnostics; secondary infections possible). Mortalities greatest July-August; 60 of 2,006 survived (3.0%).

cause_description_in_file: Two small holes (<1-2 ft diameter) found in net at harvest, allowing fish to escape
citation_and_page: FY2023 Annual Report, p. 26; Table 9 p. 27; FY2024 Annual Report, p. 29
issues: '~554 unaccounted' is an arithmetic error (1,005-454 = 551); 'consistent within rounding' is actually an exact match (551 = 437+114) but is the preparer's comparison, and both are estimates (FY2023 'presumed'; FY2024 'up to'/'likely'); FY2024 says 'several' holes vs FY2023 'two'
suggested_cause_description: Two small holes (less than a foot or two across) found in the GERE net at harvest; fish presumed to have escaped. 454 of 1,005 harvested (45.2% apparent survival vs 96.5% in GERW); about 551 fish not recovered. FY2024 report says up to 437 LRS and up to 114 SNS likely escaped (551 total).

cause_description_in_file: Geothermal water-supply quality limitations; unstable rearing temperatures fluctuating 5-6C daily
issues: Minor: report hedges cause ('likely due to'); 'loss' language (74.8%) is derived, report says hatching success ~25.2%; incubation period Apr-May inferred from spawning dates Apr 21-May 5

cause_description_in_file: Reproductive failure attributed to poor body condition from high rearing densities the prior year
issues: Report is internally inconsistent on sampling (three weeks p. 10 vs two consecutive weeks p. 11, 'end of April and May'); cause is hedged ('may have been a large factor'); date 'Early May' only partly matches
suggested_cause_description: SNS captive broodstock (CY2017) spawning attempt, late April-early May 2023: no females ovulated, males had low milt volume (<1-2 mL) and motility (<50%). Possibly related to poor body condition after high rearing densities the prior year.

cause_description_in_file: Late/colder-than-normal spring, high flows/turbidity, rapid warm/cool swings, low adult return
issues: Minor: drift netting figure is 'less than 50 fish over several nights'; dip netting was primary method

cause_description_in_file: Unusually cool water temperatures caused algae-bloom crashes -> lethal early-morning DO; exacerbated by pond-space crowding
citation_and_page: FY2024 Annual Report, p. 19; p. 24 (Table 8 stocking)
issues: 30-65% range, 45.0% best estimate and Major tier are analyst guesses (report says only 'several thousand'); 'worse than any prior year' is really FY24 summer mortality hatchery-wide being higher than ever seen; 6,039 is a derived sum and not the number at crash time
suggested_cause_description: Unusually cool water in mid-to-late August crashed algae blooms in several fingerling ponds, causing lethal early-morning DO; two noteworthy crashes (P12, P13) caused acute loss of 'several thousand fish' plus some chronic losses; likely exacerbated by crowding. No count or percent reported. Report says summer mortality was higher than ever previously seen.

cause_description_in_file: Costia (ectoparasite) infections during extended intensive tank rearing, worsened by prolonged holding due to lack of pond space
issues: 'Isolation' and 'ectoparasite' not in report; Costia share of the 2,876 not stated; 'worsened' is interpretive; species mix only 'presumably' LRS/SNS
suggested_cause_description: Observed tank mortality (2,876 fish, ~9.5% of 30,150 collected) over a ~3-month intensive rearing period in the Salvage Building, including multiple health-related mortalities from Costia infections while awaiting pond space.

cause_description_in_file: Cumulative unaccounted/unobserved mortality, attributed by staff to "cumulative human error" the longer fish are held intensively in tanks
issues: 23.0% is unobserved/unaccounted loss (30,150-2,876-20,344 = 6,930), not directly observed deaths; 'cumulative human error' is the report's 'likely cause'
suggested_cause_description: Unobserved (unaccounted) loss of 23.0% of the 30,150 collected; staff say the likely cause is cumulative human error the longer fish are raised intensively in tanks.

location: Net pen at Four Mile Canal, Agency Lake (holdover from Lower Klamath Refuge Ponds)
cause_description_in_file: Bacterial infection spread early in the holding period during a joint USGS/USFWS acoustic telemetry study
issues: 55% mortality is derived (100-45); report says 'acoustic study', mortalities occurred during tagging so not all loss clearly attributable to bacteria; pathogen not named; location is on p. 26
suggested_cause_description: Bacterial infection spread early in the holding period, causing multiple mortality events during USGS tagging for the joint USGS/USFWS acoustic study; overall survival 45%.

location: Gerber Reservoir net pens (west pen sonde)
cause_description_in_file: Continuous water-quality sonde malfunctioned, creating a ~7-week monitoring gap; when monitoring resumed, late-Aug DO dropped below 4 mg/L threshold (lowest 2.99 mg/L)
citation_and_page: FY2024 Annual Report, p. 30; p. 29; p. 31-32 (figures)
issues: '~7 weeks' is derived (50 days); 0.0% loss is observed mortality only, since 1,317 of 1,378 harvested (96%) and 6 handling deaths at harvest
suggested_cause_description: Sonde malfunction left a gap in continuous DO data from Jun 25 to the morning of Aug 14 (about 7 weeks); in late August DO fell below 4 mg/L briefly (lowest 2.99 mg/L). No sucker mortalities observed during growout.

cause_description_in_file: Cyanobacteria bloom detected (water turned light brown/turbid); no toxins found on analysis
issues: July 23 is the sample date, not necessarily bloom onset; report does not link bloom to mortality; 0.0% loss caveat (96% harvest survival)

cause_description_in_file: Unexplained mortality of non-target species (perch); cause/disease not identified; no impact to target suckers
issues: 'Non-target' and 'incidentally in net pen' not stated; 'unexplained/no cause identified' is paraphrase of 'no obvious signs of disease'; 'no impact to suckers' overstated (only no sucker mortality observed)
suggested_cause_description: Three small (~30 mm) perch were found dead in GERE on July 27 with no obvious signs of disease; no sucker mortality observed and no further mortality thereafter.
